citation: What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. (2006). WWC Intervention Report: Connect with Kids. https://www.connectwithkids.com
title: Connect with Kids lesson sequence: trait introduction, video, teacher-led discussion, and delayed follow-up activity
description: Each Connect with Kids lesson follows a recurring instructional sequence: "Each lesson begins with an introduction of the trait being taught followed by the Connect with Kids video for that trait." The video is followed by teacher-led discussion using questions from the teacher resource guide, and one to two weeks later a follow-up activity in which students practice and demonstrate behaviors associated with the trait through cooperative learning exercises. Video dosage differs by level: three video segments per trait in the middle/high school program and one video per trait in the elementary program.
requirements: Teacher resource guide with discussion questions
Connect with Kids videos for each character trait
constraints: Follow-up activity occurs one to two weeks after the video and discussion lesson, as designed
target_learners: Middle and high school students in grades 6–12
target_learning_goals: Understanding and demonstrating behaviors associated with core character traits
examples: Students practice trait behaviors through cooperative learning exercises; monthly television specials aired on local stations extend the lessons, with parents encouraged to view the shows with their child
key_sources: What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. (2006). WWC Intervention Report: Connect with Kids. https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/InterventionReport/104

article_title: Effects of CW-FIT on Teachers' Ratings of Elementary School Students at Risk for Emotional and Behavioral Disorders
citation: Caldarella, P., Larsen, R. A., Williams, L., Wills, H. P., Kamps, D., & Wehby, J. (2017). Effects of CW-FIT on teachers’ ratings of elementary school students at risk for emotional and behavioral disorders. Journal of Positive Behavior Interventions. Advance online publication. https://doi.org/10.1177/1098300717723353
title: CW-FIT multi-tiered classroom management program
description: CW-FIT (Class-wide Function-Related Intervention Teams) is a "multi-tiered classroom management program" incorporating PBIS strategies at tier 1 (social skills instruction, interdependent group contingencies, and praise) and tier 2 (self-management and help cards) to improve classroom management and student behavior during typical academic instruction. Teachers directly teach social skills in 10-min lessons, set daily point goals, use a timer at approximately 3-min intervals, divide classes into teams of two to six students, and reward teams meeting point goals. The article evaluates its effects on teacher ratings in an RCT.
requirements: Teachers receive a two-hour training session plus one to two weeks of coaching until they implement independently with fidelity as indicated by fidelity observations
constraints: The article notes fidelity of implementation matters: treatment teachers implemented CW-FIT with 92.08% fidelity, and higher fidelity was associated with better outcomes
target_learners: elementary school students at risk for emotional and behavioral disorders
target_learning_goals: appropriate social skills such as following directions, getting the teacher's attention, and ignoring inappropriate behavior
examples: Treatment teachers taught the three main social skills "Follow Directions the First Time," "How to Get the Teacher's Attention," and "Ignore Inappropriate Behavior," each with four specific steps and visual cues posted in the classroom

Effects of CW-FIT on teachers’ ratings of elementary school students at risk for emotional and behavioral disorders. Journal of Positive Behavior Interventions. article_title: Improving Students' Chinese Writing Abilities in Taiwan with the "Conditioned Writing System"
citation: Yuan-Chen Liu, Wan-Chun Lee, Tzu-Hua Huang, Hsiao-Mei Hsieh. (2012). IMPROVING STUDENTS’ CHINESE WRITING ABILITIES IN TAIWAN WITH THE “CONDITIONED WRITING SYSTEM”. TOJET: The Turkish Online Journal of Educational Technology, 11(3). https://www.tojet.net/
title: CWB online interactive writing system ("May's Writing Meadow")
description: The CWB online interactive writing system, called "May's Writing Meadow," was designed for the experimental group's seventh-grade students. Its "Writing Garden" section contains writing principles, evaluation standards, and a password-protected "Writing Practice Zone" with five units of conditioned-writing question sets. Students answer basic and advanced guidance questions, write from the topic, access expert tips and reference links, view completed work, and use a revision page to proofread and revise, receiving timely teacher feedback and peer visibility.
requirements: Students must become members and log in with an account number and password to enter the Writing Practice Zone
constraints: The system was designed for seventh-grade students in this study's ten-week Chinese essay writing program
target_learners: seventh-grade junior high school students in Taiwan learning Chinese essay writing
target_learning_goals: Chinese essay writing performance in argumentation, text organization and structure, and language use
examples: Over ten weeks students completed five CWB writing exercises, each spanning two weeks: one week to write and one week for teachers to rate the writing
key_sources: Yuan-Chen Liu, Wan-Chun Lee, Tzu-Hua Huang, Hsiao-Mei Hsieh. (2012). IMPROVING STUDENTS’ CHINESE WRITING ABILITIES IN TAIWAN WITH THE “CONDITIONED WRITING SYSTEM”. TOJET: The Turkish Online Journal of Educational Technology, 11(3). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ989211

article_title: Improving Students' Chinese Writing Abilities in Taiwan with the "Conditioned Writing System"
citation: Yuan-Chen Liu, Wan-Chun Lee, Tzu-Hua Huang, Hsiao-Mei Hsieh. (2012). IMPROVING STUDENTS’ CHINESE WRITING ABILITIES IN TAIWAN WITH THE “CONDITIONED WRITING SYSTEM”. TOJET: The Turkish Online Journal of Educational Technology, 11(3). https://www.tojet.net/
title: Ten-week progressive online writing-practice cycle with guided question sets, teacher feedback, and revision
description: The CWB curriculum organized writing practice into five two-week exercises across ten weeks: one week for students to complete a complete piece of writing and one week for teachers to rate it. Each exercise's first page presents basic guidance and advanced guidance question sets for pre-writing planning; a second page supports translating with tips and reference links; and completion and revision pages support reviewing, with timely teacher scores and suggestions. This progressive cycle gave students a sense of achievement and confidence while making revision expedient.
requirements: Suitable question sets designed according to the conditioned writing approach; teacher rating and feedback time built into each cycle
constraints: Each writing exercise was conducted for two weeks during the ten-week experiment in this study
target_learning_goals: Chinese essay writing performance across argumentation, organization, and language use
examples: Writing Exercises I–V were assigned in sequence, with question sets targeting all three assessment standards in the first two exercises and progressively focused sets thereafter

article_title: Class-Wide Function-Related Intervention Teams "CW-FIT" Efficacy Trial Outcomes
citation: Debra Kamps, Howard Wills, Harriett Dawson-Bannister, Linda Heitzman-Powell, Esther Kottwitz, Blake Hansen, and Kandace Fleming (2015). Class-Wide Function-Related Intervention Teams "CW-FIT" Efficacy Trial Outcomes. Journal of Positive Behavior Interventions. https://doi.org/10.1177/1098300714565244
title: CW-FIT group contingency classroom management program
description: CW-FIT (Class-Wide Function-Related Intervention Teams) is "a classroom management system based on teaching classroom rules/skills and use of a group contingency plan with differential reinforcement of appropriate behaviors, and minimized social attention to inappropriate behavior". It was evaluated in a 4-year randomized trial in 17 elementary schools with 159 teachers and shown to improve on-task behavior, praise, and reprimand rates.
requirements: Building coaches serving as trainers with 40% to 50% time coach assignment
Weekly feedback from building coaches and researchers based on fidelity data
constraints: Not a function-based intervention per se, in that a functional analysis was not conducted prior to implementation
Effects were based on 20 min of direct observation 1 to 2 times per week during a teacher-selected problem time
target_learners: elementary students in urban and culturally diverse schools
examples: Three target skills taught in class-wide lessons during initial 3 to 5 sessions: gaining the teacher's attention, following directions, and ignoring inappropriate behaviors

article_title: Effects of generic medical communication training on physiotherapy students' ability to communicate in movement-based clinical scenarios: a cross-sectional study.
citation: Yanase Yukiko, Hiragi Saki, Kawahara Yasuhiro. (2026). Effects of generic medical communication training on physiotherapy students’ ability to communicate in movement-based clinical scenarios: a cross-sectional study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-08560-2
title: Eight-item CWM skill assessment rubric scored by nominal group technique
description: Because no standardized scale existed for communication with movement, the authors defined eight binary-scored assessment items based on previous studies: physical contact, explanation of movement methods, checking patients' understanding, explanations using the body, pain assessment, paraphrasing technical terms, moving around patients, and explanation of test results. Final scores were aggregated by five experienced physiotherapist scorers using the nominal group technique, accepting items scored 1 by at least three of five scorers. The authors state the scale "was a preliminary operationalization of the construct, not a validated instrument," with Cronbach's alpha of 0.56.
requirements: Scoring by five experienced physiotherapists using the nominal group technique with video-recorded task performance
constraints: The rubric lacks a validated, widely accepted assessment tool; internal consistency was Cronbach's alpha 0.56
target_learning_goals: Communication with movement during physical examination tasks
examples: Scores were determined from video recordings of participants performing three standardized tests on a standardized patient simulating left hemiplegic stroke
key_sources: Yanase Yukiko, Hiragi Saki, Kawahara Yasuhiro. (2026). Effects of generic medical communication training on physiotherapy students’ ability to communicate in movement-based clinical scenarios: a cross-sectional study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-08560-2

article_title: Effects of generic medical communication training on physiotherapy students' ability to communicate in movement-based clinical scenarios: a cross-sectional study.
citation: Yanase Yukiko, Hiragi Saki, Kawahara Yasuhiro. (2026). Effects of generic medical communication training on physiotherapy students’ ability to communicate in movement-based clinical scenarios: a cross-sectional study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-08560-2
title: Communication with movement (CWM) as a distinct physiotherapy communication construct
description: The article defines communication with movement (CWM) as "communication that occurs when PTs make contact with patients’ bodies and explain physical movements." It positions CWM as a movement-specific form of non-verbal communication (kinesics) that general medical communication training does not cover, operationalized preliminarily through eight skill items ranging from physical contact to explaining test results in lay terms. The construct is grounded in prior findings that physiotherapists maintain physical contact, demonstrate movements with their own bodies, and move around patients during assessment and treatment.
requirements: Operationalization through performance tasks with standardized patients, since no standardized assessment scale exists
constraints: The construct is a preliminary operationalization; the authors state future research should establish the concept of CWM skills and confirm their role in physiotherapy education
target_learners: Physiotherapy students prior to clinical practice
target_learning_goals: Communicating during physical contact, movement instruction, and test-result explanation
examples: The CWM task combined the left thumb sense of passive movement test, the right knee extension manual muscle test, and the left lower limb motor paralysis test on a standardized patient
key_sources: Yanase Yukiko, Hiragi Saki, Kawahara Yasuhiro. (2026). Effects of generic medical communication training on physiotherapy students’ ability to communicate in movement-based clinical scenarios: a cross-sectional study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-08560-2
